metadata.case_name: NG KAI MAN SAMUEL v. CHOW YAT TAK T/A KAM KEE STEVEDORE & TRANSPORTATION CO

plaintiff.occupation_before: Crane operator / foreman (assign and supervise other crane operators and workers)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Day shift taxi driver (from 15 April 2009 until assessment); previously crane operator (1 Sep 2006–15 Nov 2006) and transportation worker (20 Jul 2007–31 Oct 2008)
plaintiff.education_level: Local education up to secondary level at Form 4

injuries.description: Right thumb distal phalanx partial amputation; loss of distal 1 cm of right thumb; widened stump end; loss of nail; fracture distal phalanx.
source: Physical examination showed distal amputation of right thumb. X-ray right thumb showed fracture distal phalanx.
Specific: Right thumb distal phalanx partial amputation.

61. Physical examination shows loss of distal 1 cm of his right thumb, widened stump end, loss of nail, reduced sensation and numbness stump end. Updated x-ray shows loss of distal 11 mm of the distal phalanx right thumb.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified traumatic amputation of thumb

manifestations.description: Pain over tip of right thumb / stump
Reduced sensation and numbness at stump end
Reduced dexterity in performing fine movements
Weakness / reduced grip strength (decreased lateral pinch and power grip)
Difficulty playing racket-sports using his right hand
Difficulty performing fine control of a crane and performing maintenance tasks (including climbing the 'cat-ladder' and carrying/using spanner and hammer)

treatments_received: Physiotherapy: Magnetopulse Therapy, Desensitization program, mobilizing, stretching and strengthening exercises (total 8 sessions).
Occupational therapy: desensitization and hand class (hand class arranged since 10-10-05).

losses.description: Physical loss of distal 1 cm of his right thumb; the thumb can no longer perform a 'locking' function to grasp objects firmly.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Will definitely encounter difficulty playing racket-sports using his right hand, but not to the extent that he is unable to participate at all.
In open market, on balance, he will not be able to resume his pre-injury job any more; it would be difficult, if not impossible, to perform fine control of a crane.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Tai Yan v Transward Stevedore Ltd. & Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: Authority bearing similar features and extent of injury as in the present one although the Plaintiff herein suffered a bit lesser.
